blurb: Hair, scalp, face, skin, eyes, teeth and grooming - the visible layer, in one sheet.

sections.title: Know Your Hair - Walker Types
intro: Type sets the wash cadence. Porosity sets the moisture strategy.
rows: Flat cuticle lying flat on a straight shaft, and sebum spreads along it without help, so the scalp stays clean on a 2-3 wash/week cadence. Lightweight, volumising formulas do no harm here; heavy oils only flatten the roots.

An S-pattern shaft with a cuticle that lifts in humidity, so frizz appears the moment the air gets damp. Wash about twice a week and use a light leave-in film; heavy cream sits on the wave instead of moving with it.

Sebum cannot travel the curl loop, so the scalp dries while the mid-lengths stay oily - the scalp decides the cadence, not the lengths. Co-wash 1-2x/week and style soaking wet; dry hair resists the curl you are trying to set.

The tightest coils and the most fragile shaft: short of scalp stretch, the pattern itself concentrates breakage at the bends. Weekly washing at most, deep conditioning, protective styles, and satin at the pillow.

sections.title: Porosity - the Float Test
rows: A tightly sealed cuticle, so water beads off and products sit on the surface. Apply to damp rather than soaking hair, keep to lighter oils, and skip butters that never melt.
Products absorb and are retained; the easiest hair to keep. Maintain the routine and resist the urge to add a step every time something feels flat.
An over-processed, open cuticle that takes water instantly and loses it just as fast. Deep condition, use protein treatments to rebuild the cortex, drop the heat, and stop bleaching.

sections.title: Androgenetic Alopecia - the Norwood Map
intro: Act early. Follicular miniaturisation is gradual: you lose pigment and shaft diameter before you lose count, so every stage before N3 still carries recoverable hair.
rows: A normal hairline with no temple recession and nothing to treat. Photograph the hairline and the vertex now, standardised, so you have a baseline to compare against in five years instead of a memory.
Roughly 1-3 cm of recession at each temple with the frontal hairline still intact and miniaturised hairs still present at the margin. DHT blockade plus minoxidil can still restore density here.

Frontotemporal recession joins across the frontal hairline so the line forms a shallow M, usually with vertex thinning beginning too. This is the last stage at which minoxidil reliably regrows a visible frontal hairline.

Bald frontotemporal quarters with the vertex still full, giving the inverted-V pattern. The frontal margin is now scarred miniaturised hair, so treat the vertex and stabilise - regrowing a temple from here is not the expectation.
A single island of vertex hair left between bald temples and a thinning crown. Vertex responds best to finasteride and minoxidil, so this is the stage where treatment still pays visibly.

The vertex is the last hair standing and is now thinning as well. This is where a transplant genuinely changes the reflection in a window - but only once the loss is stabilised, and only if the donor zone still holds terminal hair worth taking, because the crown at N6 is past what finasteride or minoxidil alone can rescue.

sections.title: Scalp Disorders - Do Not Confuse Them
intro: An antifungal treats Malassezia. Minoxidil and finasteride treat DHT. Confusing the two costs years.
rows: Itchy, flaking scalp driven by Malassezia digesting sebum. Zinc pyrithione or ketoconazole 2% shampoo twice weekly clears it. It is not hair loss, and treating it as hair loss means years of the wrong product.

Patterned thinning at the temples and vertex with miniaturised, still-pigmented hairs, no inflammation and no flaking. Treated with minoxidil and DHT blockade; treating it with an antifungal does nothing at all.

More than about 100 hairs per wash spread across the whole head, with no patterned loss. Onset lags 8-12 weeks behind the trigger and resolution takes 3-6 months after it is removed. No drug fixes a deficiency, a fever or a shock.

The most common reversible driver of a diffuse shed, and the one no amount of minoxidil will touch. With ferritin already low on your profile, treat the iron - and pair it with the protein and vitamin C that let it get used - rather than escalating a drug.

Well-demarcated non-scarring patches with nail pitting and exclamation-mark hairs at the margin - an autoimmune process, not a hygiene problem. Needs systemic consideration, not minoxidil monotherapy.

Sustained tension from tight styles pulls follicles into scar; the FDA label lists it as a cause of hair loss. Unlike AGA it does not respond to minoxidil or finasteride, because the follicles are gone rather than asleep.

sections.title: The Hair Drug Stack
rows: Topical minoxidil - apply it to the scalp

The target is the follicle, not the hair: on a shaft it is pharmacologically inert and the vehicle only wicks drug to skin. Part the hair, expose the thinning scalp, drip it on, and do not lather or massage it in. FDA OTC label.
1 mL is the ceiling, not a floor

The dose-response plateaus. The label is explicit that using more or more often will not improve results - it only adds scalp irritation, flaking and cost. 5% once daily is equivalent to 2% twice daily, so the twice-daily habit buys no extra hair.
Allow 2-4 hours of dry time before bed

Wet product transfers to pillows, hats and partners - transfer causes hypertrichosis on their arms and face and halves your own absorbed dose. Wash your hands, separate towels and pillowcases, and let it dry fully.

Minoxidil shortens telogen from about 20 days to 1-2 in rat data, dumping hairs that would have shed later while prolonging anagen. Shedding starts at 2-4 weeks and lasts 3-6. Recognise it as the drug working, not as progressive loss. JAAD Int 2024.
Judge minoxidil at 6 months, not 8 weeks

The label allows 2 to 4 months for visible results and warns it will not work for everyone. Set a 6-month trial and judge on 12-month photo-trichoscopy. Quitting during the shed window is the single commonest way to lose the benefit you paid for.

Low-dose oral minoxidil is off-label for hair, so it needs a prescriber and a baseline blood pressure including orthostatics, plus heart rate and an echo or ECG if you are over 40 or have cardiac history. Across 1,404 patients: hypertrichosis ~15%, lightheadedness 1.7%, fluid retention 1.3%, tachycardia 0.9%. In men, 1.25-2.5 mg daily is the usual range.
Overlap topical when you start oral

Starting both from zero doubles the shedding load, and dread shed is the top discontinuation reason. If you are already on topical, keep it going when you start low-dose oral to blunt the shed - do not go in clean.

Phase 3 delivered +20.2 hairs versus placebo with roughly 100-fold lower plasma levels than the oral tablet. Sexual adverse events were 2.8% topical versus 3.3% placebo versus 4.8% oral - low, but not zero, so it still gets a proper discussion.

Prescribed for male pattern hair loss. Expect 2-6 months, judge at 12, and note that hair counts stay above baseline to 5 years while the placebo arm loses hair. Meta-analysis of 4,495 men puts the risk of sexual dysfunction at 1.55-1.66x.

5 mg is the benign-prostatic-hyperplasia dose: about five times the systemic exposure and more sexual adverse events - impotence 12.2% in year 1 rising to 22.6% by year 5 in the 1 mg label data. The label also states that efficacy in bitemporal recession has not been established; it works on vertex.

Twice weekly for four weeks for seborrhoeic dermatitis, then once a week to once every two weeks. Twice weekly is the studied frequency; daily use buys no faster clearance and costs dryness, abnormal hair texture and irritation.
Daily ketoconazole costs you your curl

Chronic daily use of the 2% antifungal produces dryness, abnormal hair texture, curl loss and discolouration, and it does this to types 3 and 4 hardest - the hair least able to tolerate an aggressive wash cadence is the hair most often told to use it daily. Fix the frequency, not the shampoo.
Ketoconazole is an adjunct, not a replacement

The systematic review found hair-shaft diameter and anagen data only, no strong randomised trial, and concluded RCTs are needed. It treats Malassezia-driven inflammation; it does not block DHT and it will not hold a receded hairline.

0.5-1.5 mm every 2-4 weeks; controlled trials report gains of +12.5 versus +1.89 hairs per square inch against the same interval of nothing. Going deeper than 1.5-2 mm buys bleeding, infection, keloid in predisposed skin and post-inflammatory pigment. Sun-protect for 48 hours after.

Small uncontrolled trials only: four minutes a day for 24 weeks in nine men moved shaft thickness from 0.085 to 0.092 mm with NOGGIN/BMP4/SMAD4 upregulation. Expect thickness, not regrowth, and do not spend on a device to do it.

Biotin deficiency is rare and the highest-quality double-blind trial found no difference versus placebo. Worse, it interferes with lab immunoassays - troponin and thyroid - and has produced false cardiac and thyroid results. Test if you are genuinely at risk (bariatric surgery, anticonvulsants, malnutrition), otherwise stop it before your next blood panel.

A transplant moves follicles; it does not create them, so the ceiling is donor density and the surgery is worthless if the crown is still miniaturising. Stabilise on finasteride and minoxidil, take the standardised photos, then reassess what the donor zone can actually carry.

sections.title: Hair Hygiene
intro: The damage driver is mechanical. Everything below is force, heat or chemistry.
rows: Daily washing does not cause hair loss

Washing removes hairs already in telogen, so the count rises for a few days and then normalises, and it does not damage follicles. Wash to the frequency your type needs; the fear is what makes people shampoo once a week and scratch their scalp instead.
Coily hair - a 2-3 week minimum between washes

Tight coils trap sebum, so the scalp of type 4 hair gets dirty without being oily at the surface. Washing every 2-3 weeks at minimum protects the scalp; daily washing is not neutral here - it strips what little lipid reaches the roots and tightens the pattern further.
Curl and coil - co-wash, not detergent

Sulfate detergents strip the cuticle on a curly or coily shaft, which is already lifted at the bend, and the pattern does not spring back. This is the types 3 and 4 rule: co-wash once or twice a week with a conditioner-based cleanse to keep the pattern and the scalp at the same time.
Press and blot - never rub with a towel

Friction plus compressive force drives cuticle sliding, cuticle-cortex interface failure, intercellular cracks and snap-back breakage - documented by scanning electron microscopy and X-ray tomography. Microfiber or plush towel, press and blot, or air-dry.

Hot tools disrupt the disulfide bonds in keratin, and the damage is cumulative on the cuticle rather than obvious at any one session. Lower frequency, heat protectant, air-dry whenever the style allows it.

Hair is at its most fragile when wet and dry detangling with any tool maximises intercellular crack propagation. Condition or leave-in first, then a wide-tooth comb or your fingers, working in sections rather than from the ends inward at speed.

Sustained tension from cornrows, tight ponytails and headset use converts follicles to scar, and the FDA label lists it as a cause of hair loss. Loose styles, no prolonged tight tension - this is the one hair-loss cause where prevention is the entire treatment.
Relaxers, bleach and the follicular burn

Alkaline and oxidative processing dissolves the cuticle into porosity and breakage, and repeated chemical burn reaches scarring alopecia. Reduce frequency, deep-condition, and never stack a relaxer with a high-tension style in the same period.
Protective styles need a satin finish

A tight style transfers friction to the scalp all night, and cotton against cotton is the roughest surface available - which is why this matters for types 3 and 4 whose whole protective strategy depends on it. A satin or cotton-lined wrap and a satin pillowcase keep the coil intact instead of grinding it against the cuticle.

The damage driver is mechanical cuticle damage and cleansing frequency, not the surfactant label. Dogmatic avoidance produces over-product buildup and clarifying-shampoo overuse, which is worse than the thing it was avoiding. Target sebum by hair type.
The scalp is a sun-exposed site

UV mutates follicles and accelerates the inflammation around the miniaturised follicles of androgenetic alopecia. Hat plus SPF 30+ on the parting and the nape - not optional once the crown has thinned and the skin shows through.
Helmets and hats - cover the interface

Chronic friction plus UV at the hairline is traction plus photo-inflammation at the exact site that recedes first. A helmet liner that covers the hairline, and a hat on the motorcycle in summer, cost nothing against the alternatives.
Dandruff shampoo twice a week, not daily

Zinc pyrithione or ketoconazole 2% twice weekly clears seborrhoeic dermatitis. Daily use adds irritation and flaking without clearing it sooner, and it strips the scalp of the lipids that keep the margin comfortable.
Trichotillomania - treat the pulling, not the fallout

A DSM-5 impulse- and OCD-related disorder, and untreated it causes permanent follicular damage. Cognitive behavioural therapy with habit reversal beats clomipramine; screen for it instead of escalating minoxidil on a scalp that will never respond.

sections.title: The Workup Before Any Hair Drug
intro: Diffuse shedding is a laboratory question first and a prescription question second.
rows: Iron deficiency is a real and fully reversible driver of diffuse shedding, and no amount of minoxidil fixes it - women carry the higher prevalence, but men are not spared. Test ferritin and transferrin saturation together before touching iron. In men there is no menstrual blood loss to explain a low ferritin, and hereditary haemochromatosis typically presents in mid-life with ferritin above 300.
Ferritin in women is confounded by menstrual loss

Menstrual blood loss lowers ferritin in otherwise healthy women, so a low result is expected and a weak hair signal. Interpret it with menstrual status and CRP - ferritin is an acute-phase reactant and infection or inflammation inflates it - before attributing shed to iron.

B12 deficiency causes true telogen effluvium and no drug corrects a deficiency. Methylmalonic acid is the marker that separates B12 from folate deficiency, which is why the pair beats a B12 level alone.
Thyroid disease is a classic reversible cause of diffuse shedding, and both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism do it. It is a single line on a blood panel that is otherwise being run anyway.

Zinc deficiency disturbs the follicle, as does copper excess and long-term high-dose zinc. For vitamin D, context beats a number: the 2024 Endocrine Society retracted the 'sufficient above 30 ng/mL' category, so treat below 12-20 ng/mL and stop chasing the boundary.

More than 60 hairs per wash plus miniaturised hairs separates the three diagnoses that otherwise blur: over 10% vellus is androgenetic alopecia, under 10% is telogen effluvium, under 100 hairs with under 10% vellus is normal.

Shedding starts 8-12 weeks after the insult and resolves 3-6 months after the trigger is removed. A sudden-looking shed in spring is usually last autumn's crash diet, illness or bereavement - which is also why the intervention only works if you can find the date.

A fast deficit is an insult like any other, and the shed arrives 8-12 weeks later - which means the hair loss you notice in month two of a cut usually began in month zero of it. Cut at 0.5-1% a week, keep protein high, and expect the timeline to be the mirror image of the timeline you set.
A bulk hides the shed the cut reveals

During a surplus, overall density masks a stress-driven shed rather than stopping it - and the deficit that ends the bulk exposes it 8-12 weeks later, where it gets blamed on the cut. Photograph on a fixed schedule through both phases so the timeline is visible instead of remembered.
Trichodynia is a stress red flag

Painful scalp reported in 29% of hair-loss patients against 3.3% of controls, with psychopathology in 76% of those assessed. Tenderness plus sudden diffuse shed means look for stress, sleep debt and a hard few months - not for a better shampoo.

sections.title: Jawline Reality
rows: Fat is the mask, bone is the floor

The buccal fat pad increases from childhood into adulthood and may not begin to decrease until 60-70, when it descends and pseudo-herniates - while midface fat overall falls about 12% a decade (superficial -11.3%, deep -18.4%). Know which compartment you are actually chasing before you spend anything.
Submental and buccal fat leave last

In a deficit the jawline is not where the first fat leaves. Cutting harder for definition usually hollows the midface and the eyes first, because those compartments are already declining with age whatever your body fat is doing.

No credible human evidence of jawline remodelling. The AAO explicitly warns against it (January 2024): risks include tooth loosening, bite misalignment, tooth wear and speech impairment. Stop, and get an orthodontic or orthognathic assessment if function bothers you.
Orthodontics moves the smile, not the whole face
Orthodontic treatment improves facial attractiveness by only about 9% versus untreated controls - a weak effect, which means it is worth doing for the bite and the function, not as a jawline lever.
Buccal fat removal on a lean face

Buccal fat is described as maintaining consistent volume through life, and its loss is neither needed nor desirable in thin or gaunt faces - removal there causes premature ageing. Body fat first; surgical consultation only if the lower third is genuinely full.
Masseter Botox is for hypertrophy, not for the joint

Chronic clenching thickens the masseter and widens the lower face. The evidence is good for masseter hypertrophy and aesthetic narrowing, equivocal for myogenous TMD and weak for articular joint disorders. Conservative management first: splint, physio, awareness training.

sections.title: The Face and Skin Stack - Four Products Do 95% of the Work
intro: Cleanse, retinoid, SPF, moisturise. Everything else on this sheet is supporting cast.
rows: Over-cleansing strips lipids and raises transepidermal water loss. A second cleanse only earns its place when the first did not remove sunscreen or heavy sebum, and hot water strips lipids while ice causes vasoconstriction followed by reactive vasodilation.
The only topical category with repeatable evidence for photoageing texture and for the fine lines retinisation actually reverses. Everything else on this sheet exists to make this one tolerable.
Cumulative UV exposure is the dominant modulator of how your skin looks at sixty; no serum outruns it. This is the row that compounds while you do nothing else.
Barrier lipids plus a humectant keep water in the stratum corneum and hold transepidermal water loss down, which is what makes a retinoid and an acid tolerable enough to keep using.
Fitzpatrick I - the burner is your readout
Type I skin burns before it tans, so erythema is the cheapest damage signal you will ever get. Daily SPF 30+ from childhood, and treat every burn as a dose of damage rather than a tan.
Fitzpatrick II - actinic damage arrives early

Light skin tints lightly but burns easily, and with no pigment buffer the cumulative UVA damage reads as lines and dyschromia almost as soon as you stop covering up. Daily SPF 30+, tinted if you pigment, retinoid from your late twenties.
Fitzpatrick III - tans, and still ages

Tanning is a UVA response, not protection - the damage still arrives on schedule. In this range acne scarring is often a colour problem before it is a texture problem: the marks fade over months, the pits do not. Control acne early and you prevent both.
Fitzpatrick IV - pigment is the damage readout

In this range every inflammation leaves a visible mark, so anything that stings will show. Daily tinted iron-oxide SPF, a slow retinoid ramp, and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation treated as prevention rather than damage.
Fitzpatrick V - tinted SPF is not optional

Visible light at 415-530 nm and heat at 33-34 degrees both induce pigmentation in this range. Zinc oxide and titanium dioxide alone block UV and not visible light; only iron-oxide pigments close that door, which is what a tinted product does.
Fitzpatrick VI - the procedure tax is pigment

Highest risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and of keloid at any wound. Tinted SPF daily, and no in-office peel, laser or deep microneedling by anyone who does not treat your skin type routinely. Slow is the strategy that keeps you uninjured.

sections.title: Retinoids
rows: The potency ladder is stepwise, not exponential

retinol -> retinal -> retinoic acid. Retinal is about 1x more potent than retinol, not 10x or 100x; conversion steps are not multiples. Judge by tolerance, adherence and 6-12 months of duration, which is where every retinoid trial is won or lost.

Retinoids thin the stratum corneum and interfere with epidermal lipid synthesis, raising water loss and causing the irritant dermatitis people mistake for purging. Damp skin increases the penetration rate and therefore the irritant load - wait at least 20 minutes after cleansing.
Every third night for two weeks, then build

Irritation severity is dose-dependent, so climb over 6-8 weeks: third night for a fortnight, then every other night, then nightly. Short-contact therapy - apply, leave five minutes, rinse - is the faster route to tolerance if you want it.

Moisturiser, then retinoid, then moisturiser. It measurably reduces irritation and it does NOT reduce efficacy - the fear that buffering makes the retinoid useless is wrong, and it is the single best change for anyone whose skin flares on a bare application.

Purging: comedonal lesions ahead of the treated area, resolving in 4-6 weeks, no burning. Irritation: burning and stinging, no comedones, can appear anywhere on the face. If it burns, stop for 3-5 days, restart less often and add barrier support.
One new active at a time, 6-8 weeks apart

Retinoid plus AHA plus BHA plus vitamin C plus benzoyl peroxide on a compromised barrier is how you get retinoid dermatitis mislabelled as purging and then abandoned. Introduce one thing, wait 6-8 weeks, then introduce the next.
Never a retinoid without daily SPF

Retinoids are photosensitive, especially to UVA, and the combination amplifies photodamage - so treating photoageing while unprotected can make it worse. Daily broad-spectrum SPF is not optional and the retinoid belongs at night.
Adapalene for acne, tretinoin for texture

Adapalene 0.1% is better tolerated than tretinoin 0.025% in men and is the acne first line - but it is not licensed for anti-ageing and the photoageing evidence is thinner. Route it: adapalene for acne and oily skin, tretinoin or OTC retinal for texture.
Tazarotene is not the gentler option

Tazarotene is more irritant than tretinoin, not less, and it is teratogenic. If a retinoid is going to be avoided on irritation grounds, adapalene or OTC retinal are the retreat, not the strongest prescription in the cupboard.
Retinoids at night, never in the morning
They are light-sensitive and unstable in the presence of oxygen and light, so a daytime retinoid is a mistake twice over - less active and more irritated. Night application on dry skin, morning SPF.

Topical retinoids are contraindicated in pregnancy, tazarotene carries a boxed pregnancy warning and isotretinoin is teratogenic; finasteride is contraindicated too. If you are pregnant or planning, stop and tell your prescriber rather than pausing for a month.

sections.title: Sunscreen
intro: The labelled SPF is a lab number. Here is what actually lands on your face.
rows: Two milligrams per square centimetre is the labelled dose

That is what earns the number on the bottle. Real users apply 25-50% of it, so after one application the effective SPF is about 3.2 - and UV-transmitting products deliver only roughly 59% of label SPF and 42% of label UVA. Schalka 2009; ISO 24443.
Two finger-lengths for the face, one ounce for the body
The only unit that survives contact with a real bathroom and a real morning. Measure it once with the bottle until you can eyeball it, because a 40 ml dot is a third of what you need.
Protection decays with time, sweat and bathing, and the film does not even out on its own - it thins where you touched it. A stick for reapplication works in the places a cream never gets reapplied.
UVA walks through car and office glass
Glass blocks UVB; UVA largely passes. If you sit beside a window or drive in daylight you are exposed on every weekday you believed you were indoors, which is most of them.
Visible light drives pigment, not just UV

Blue light at 415-530 nm induces pigmentation in darker skin and so does heat at 33-34 degrees. A plain mineral sunscreen blocks UV and not visible light; only iron-oxide pigments close that route, which is what a tinted product does.
Treat neck, ears, hands, scalp and upper chest
These are the sun-exposed sites that age, and neck sun damage reads as a tan line that gives your age away from across a room. SPF on all of them daily, and on the parting line once the scalp shows.

Film-formers and UV filters degrade with heat and oxidation, so a dashboard bottle in July is a decoration. Check the period-after-opening date and store it under 25 degrees; buy the size you will finish before the date.
Mineral versus chemical is a vehicle choice

Mineral filters leave a white cast and are photostable; modern chemical filters are efficient and well tolerated. Neither is categorically harmful and zinc oxide does not cause hyperpigmentation. Pick on skin type, vehicle and adherence - the best sunscreen is the one you actually reapply.

Deliberate UVA exposure is photoageing by definition, and the IARC classifies it as a Group 1 carcinogen with roughly 1,400-fold higher melanoma risk. There is no safe tanning and no base tan that makes a summer one safer.
Dark circles are rarely a cream deficiency

The commonest causes are post-inflammatory pigment, vascular, dermal thinning, allergic rhinitis, sleep deprivation, iron deficiency and smoking - eye creams do almost nothing for most of them. Evaluate the cause before you buy anything.
Retinoids on the eyelid and contact lenses

Periorbital skin is the thinnest on the face, so retinoid dermatitis there is common and can leave periorbital pigment. Apply to the orbital bone, never the lid margin. Separately, retinoids and isotretinoin dry the eye - cut contact-lens hours and use preservative-free drops.

sections.title: Skin Types and Conditions
rows: Fitzpatrick I - actives are visible immediately

You can usually tolerate stronger actives, and the risk profile flips the other way: lasers and deep peels more often leave hypopigmentation than pigment on this range. A pale patch that does not return its colour is your stop signal, not a tan line.
Fitzpatrick II - start actinic control before 30

With no pigment buffer, cumulative damage on this range reads as fine lines and telangiectasia earlier than elsewhere, and there is nothing to hide it with. Daily SPF plus a retinoid from the late twenties is prevention, not correction.
Fitzpatrick III - acne scarring is colour before texture

Post-acne pigment fades over months while the pits do not remodel much at all, so early control of the inflammation prevents the permanent half of the problem. Retinoid and SPF do more for the pigment than any brightening product.
Fitzpatrick IV - assume every procedure will pigment

In this range any inflammation or wound can leave a visible mark for months, which makes aftercare part of the procedure rather than an optional extra. Daily tinted SPF before and after, and no stacking of actives around a treatment window.
Fitzpatrick V - heat and blue light are the triggers

Melanosomes are larger and more dispersed in this range, so heat at 33-34 degrees and visible light at 415-530 nm both switch pigmentation on. Tinted iron-oxide SPF daily plus a trigger log beats guessing which product did it.
Fitzpatrick VI - keloid and pigment are the price

Any wound in this range carries a real chance of a keloid or of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, which rules out unsupervised peels, lasers and microneedling beyond 1.5 mm. Treat only with someone who treats your skin type routinely, and expect weeks of aftercare.

Persistent central-face redness with flushing and papules or pustules. The one absolute rule is that no steroid ever touches it: steroids produce steroid-induced rosacea, skin atrophy, striae and a rebound flare on stopping, documented in series averaging 0.25 to 20 years of use.

Alcohol is among the most reliable rosacea triggers - vasodilation, histamine and a compromised barrier all at once - and it stacks with hot drinks, spicy food and heat. Triggers act at any dose, so log alcohol against your flare days rather than treating the redness as a skin problem only.

Fine papules around the mouth, nose and eyes with a burning rim, and almost always steroid-induced or driven by an over-active combination product. Stop every steroid and every active; the flare runs for weeks after they are gone, which is the price of the cure.

Monomorphic papules on hairy skin that do not respond to antibiotics, because nothing bacterial is happening. Ketoconazole 2% as a wash treats it - and the diagnosis is the point, since a month of the wrong antibiotic makes it worse.

Hormonal and pregnancy-associated melasma is driven by melanocytes carrying larger, more dispersed melanosomes, so heat, hormones and visible light all switch them on. Tinted iron-oxide SPF plus a blue-light blocker is the standard of care; hydroquinone is not a long-term OTC answer, because exogenous ochronosis was documented with a median 5 years of use and cases at only 2% for three months - and it is irreversible.

Every spot, burn, wax, friction site and dropped retinoid leaves a mark that takes longer to clear than the cause took to appear. Treat the inflammation and the pigment fades on its own schedule - it is a record of what happened, not a stain you can scrub off.
Dark circles with iron deficiency on the profile

Iron deficiency is one of the most common and most overlooked causes of dark circles, and it is also a cause of shedding. With Anaemia or LowFerritin already flagged, get iron studies and treat the cause before spending on an eye product that cannot reach it.
Anhidrosis - no sweat, no evaporative cooling

Without sweat, core temperature climbs fast in heat and the skin becomes hot, red and painful where friction adds to it. Keep evaporative cooling - light loose layers, wet clothing, a fan - hydrate, and see a clinician before any anticholinergic or supplement marketed as a sweat blocker, because those have their own heat-illness profile.

sections.title: Barrier Damage
intro: Almost all of this is self-inflicted, and all of it is reversible in weeks once you simplify.
rows: Over-exfoliation is the commonest self-inflicted wound

AHA plus BHA plus a scrub plus a cleansing brush plus a retinoid is barrier disruption: water loss up, stinging, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and rebound oiliness. One exfoliant, twice a week at most, and stop the moment it stings.

Retinoid dermatitis shows as dryness, peeling and burning without comedones, and it can appear away from the treated area; purging produces comedones ahead of the treated area and resolves in 4-6 weeks. If it burns, it is not purging - back off.

It oxidises fabric - white pillowcases go grey - and it is a common contact allergen at roughly 2-5% patch-test positivity. Use it on acne rather than everywhere, and note that a 2.5% wash is often better tolerated than the 10% gel that everyone buys.
Vitamin C needs pH below 3.5 and an opaque bottle

L-ascorbic acid is charged and hydrophilic, so it penetrates the stratum corneum poorly, and it oxidises to dehydroascorbic acid - the yellow in the bottle - unless the formula is acidic with vitamin E and ferulic acid in airless packaging. Derivatives such as SAP, MAP, THDA and AG do not raise skin ascorbic acid at all.

Above 5% it flushes and burns and sensitises you to everything else you add afterwards. At 2-5% it does genuinely improve barrier lipids and reduce sebum, so it is worth using - just not at the 10% that dominates the shelf.

Allergic contact dermatitis is a type IV delayed reaction at 48-72 hours, and it mimics rosacea and seborrhoeic dermatitis perfectly. Fragrance, botanicals, essential oils and benzalkonium stack invisibly across products, so the flare points at the last thing you bought rather than the one causing it.

Buclomethasone, betamethasone and fairness creams produce steroid-induced rosacea, skin atrophy, striae and a rebound flare on cessation - documented series averaged 0.25 to 20 years of use. Never unsupervised, and super-potent steroids are contraindicated on the face entirely.
Simplify to three products and rebuild

Cleanse, one active, moisturise - then reintroduce one product every 6-8 weeks and watch for 72 hours, which is roughly when a type IV allergy shows itself. A routine you cannot debug is not a routine; three products you trust beat nine you have stopped using.

sections.title: Procedures
intro: Conservative first, then the least invasive thing that could work, then only what a clinician supervises.
rows: Glycolic and lactic peels work on the stratum corneum and epidermis. They cannot reach fat, muscle or bone, so a deep peel sold as a lift is not one. Expect several days of flaking, a course rather than a single session, and a real pigment risk in the deeper skin types.

A controlled-injury procedure, so it buys texture and density - never the removal of an established scar, and never a new hairline. On the face it is aimed at texture and at shallow, rolling-acne change; on the scalp at density and shaft diameter, which is the dosing and interval row in the drug stack. Either way the effect accrues over a course, so judge it at 3-6 months rather than after one session.

Both target melanin or blood, which makes them excellent for pigment, vascular lesions and hair removal and useless for fat and for sagging. In darker skin the risk flips from too little effect to post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation or permanent hypopigmentation, so the operator's experience with your skin type is the whole decision.

They restore volume age removed, and then the effect is gone in 6-18 months while the maintenance continues indefinitely. The failure mode is overfilling a face whose midface fat is already falling about 12% a decade, which is what produces the over-filled look people recognise instantly.

A muscle-relaxing injection, not a treatment of what is tightening the muscle - whatever is driving the clenching is still there on day one, which is why the result is measured in months rather than years. The dose is titrated in units to the muscle rather than given as a fixed amount, the effect lasts a few months, and the masseter re-hypertrophies as it wears off. So it is a repeat-injection commitment on a schedule you set, with cumulative cost and a diminishing tolerance - not a one-off.

One operation rather than a course, and the decision it forces is when to go to theatre - which is only once medical treatment has stopped changing the picture. A transplant cannot create follicles and cannot recover an area that has scarred; it can only place the ones that exist. Expect nothing to look right at three months: grafted hair often sheds in the first fortnight, regrows visibly from about six months and settles by 12-18, so the verdict is due at 18 and not before. Afterwards there is nothing to top up and nothing to reschedule - but the drugs continue for the surrounding hair, which is where the real maintenance lives.

Expect the risk to be keloid and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation rather than a poor response. Assume anything that opens skin is a decision for a clinician who treats your skin type routinely, and plan weeks of sunscreen aftercare as part of the procedure, not an afterthought.

Every procedure above has a cheaper, reversible first line: sunscreen and a retinoid before any peel or laser, a night guard before Botox, and minoxidil plus finasteride before a transplant. Start there, photograph the result, and only then decide whether an intervention can beat what you already have.

No randomised trial, no INCI list, no regulator and occasional contamination. Undocumented stem cells, exosomes, snake venom peptides and unnamed acids all fail the same three questions: what is the molecule, at what concentration, and which regulator approved it.

sections.title: Teeth - Daily Hygiene
rows: Electric brush, two minutes, twice daily

Two minutes at feather pressure of about 150-250 g is the effective dose. Cervical abrasion is multifactorial - technique plus abrasive dentifrice plus force - so the fix is all three, not just the brush head you keep replacing.

Modified Bass targets the sulcus: bristles at 45 degrees into the gingival margin with gentle vibratory strokes. You are cleaning the gumline, not polishing the crowns, and the difference shows up as bleeding that stops within two weeks.

Acid softens and demineralises enamel, and abrasive brushing then removes it: in-situ enamel loss rose from 45 to 79 micrometres when brushing followed an acidic drink. Wait 30-60 minutes, rinse with water, and use a fluoridated paste - fluoride cut the loss back to 41-51 micrometres.
Fluoride at 1,350-1,500 ppm - spit, do not rinse

Fluoride is the single largest proven contributor to the global decline in caries (WHO) and there is no credible toxicity at standard exposure. Rinsing with water after brushing washes the fluoride straight back off the teeth you just protected.

Interproximal sites cause most adult in-between-tooth caries, and brushes or floss outperform brushing alone. Size an interdental brush to the embrasure rather than forcing the largest one through, and do it every evening.
Cervical abrasion - men carry it at twice the rate

Males show about twice the prevalence of cervical abrasion, 42.8% versus 23.9% with an odds ratio of 3.80, and combined horizontal plus vertical stroking carries an odds ratio of 2.20. Softer bristles, less force, and a dentifrice relative abrasive dentifrice around 100.
Bleeding gums are inflammation, not hardness

Gingivitis is reversible; periodontitis is attachment and bone loss and it is not. Bleeding on brushing or probing that persists beyond two weeks, or any mobility, recession or bone change, is a dentist appointment rather than a harder brush.
Smoking cessation is the highest-yield oral intervention

Smoking is the strongest common risk factor for periodontal attachment loss and for oral cancer, and snus leaves lesions at the placement site. No mouthwash, no whitening product and no hygienist substitutes for stopping, which is why it belongs at the top of this sheet.

Caries is driven by the frequency of pH drops rather than the total sugar load - frequent sipping keeps plaque pH below critical over and over. Keep fermentable-carbohydrate exposures to two or three meals plus water, and let the teeth clear between them.
Acidic drinks, energy drinks and sports drinks

Low pH plus sucrose plus citric acid produces erosion and caries at once - the highest erosion-risk beverage class there is. Water as the default, a straw for acidic drinks so the acid bypasses the enamel, and a rinse afterwards.

Cochrane supports a modest but real caries benefit from xylitol or sorbitol gum used twice daily. Many gums use sucrose instead, which does the opposite of what you wanted from chewing something between meals.
Oil pulling is an adjunct at best

Twenty-five RCTs and 1,184 participants: gingival indices improve, with a mean gingival index standardised mean difference of -1.14, but chlorhexidine beats it on plaque and the GRADE certainty of that evidence is very low. There is no caries-outcome data and it never replaces brushing.

Saliva is the primary remineralising buffer on the tooth surface, so xerostomia is the strongest salivary driver of caries, and alcohol-containing rinses make it worse. The effect is dose-dependent rather than confined to heavy drinkers, so water between drinks matters more than any mouthwash brand.

Hyperglycaemia impairs neutrophil function and raises both the risk and the progression of periodontal disease, while periodontal inflammation worsens glycaemic control in the other direction. With Prediabetes flagged, shorten the dental recall interval rather than treating it as optional.
Glucose, glycation and the collagen in your face

Advanced glycation end-products crosslink collagen and elastin in the dermis, stiffening it and cutting elasticity - the same chemistry that shows up as glycated haemoglobin. Better glycaemic control is a skin intervention, and it compounds with sunscreen and a retinoid rather than competing with them.

sections.title: Teeth - Whitening Ranked by Enamel Safety
rows: Sensitivity is the price of peroxide

Transient sensitivity occurs in up to two-thirds of at-home whitening users and rises with peroxide concentration and with pre-existing gingival recession. In office, 74% reported sensitivity with 35% hydrogen peroxide against 44% with 6% - so ask what concentration you are being offered.
Treat the gingivitis before you bleach

Inflamed, bleeding tissue bleeds through the tray and the gel concentrates on it, and active caries progresses and stains restorations under a whitening gel. Dental clearance and healthy gums first - whitening a dirty mouth is expensive and pointless.

A dentist-issued custom tray keeps the gel on the teeth; generic trays concentrate it on the gums, and 7-12% peroxide left on overnight penetrates the pulp. Follow the label time rather than the tube's optimism, and use a potassium-nitrate or high-fluoride desensitising paste through the course.

Charcoal is a high-abrasivity dentifrice that adsorbs stain and can increase abrasion; acid kits take the erosion route instead. Whitening changes tooth colour, not enamel mineral status - there is no whiter-than-white, only a dissolved one.

sections.title: Teeth - Alignment and Function
rows: They move teeth predictably for mild to moderate crowding and they come out, which is the entire hygiene advantage and the entire compliance risk: 20-22 hours a day or nothing happens, and the attachment is lost daily.
Fixed braces for what aligners cannot do

Root rotation, vertical control, some skeletal cases and extraction cases need a fixed appliance. Aligners are a tool rather than a superior appliance by default, and the right choice depends on the tooth movement, not the marketing.

Teeth move for the rest of your life and bone remodels around a retainer continuously, so orthodontics buys a retainer schedule rather than a result. A lost retainer means a returning tooth within months, which is the single most under-discussed fact in the consult.

Clenching and grinding cause attrition, abfraction, fractured restorations, masseter hypertrophy and temporomandibular disorder, and prevalence runs 8-31% of adults. A night guard protects the teeth from the consequences but does nothing about the drive behind the clenching.

With sleep apnoea on your profile, treat the airway as well as the teeth: apnoea fragments sleep and the arousal-driven jaw activity that follows is a driver of the grinding itself, which is why a night guard on its own keeps treating the consequence.

Chronic mouth breathing dries the mouth, worsens gingivitis and snoring, and in children drives adenoidal facies and reduced maxillary development. Self-applied jaw-forward posture carries condylar and TMD risk, so treat the obstruction - ENT and sleep assessment - rather than the posture.
Scraper frequency does not reduce caries when brushing is adequate, and rough scraping harms the tongue. Clean gently if it is coated, and spend the effort on the brush and the fluoride instead.

sections.title: Grooming Cadence
intro: A fixed date in the calendar beats motivation every time. Maintenance is the whole game.
rows: Haircuts, beard trims, nail clips and brow tidy-ups all fail on inspiration. Put them in the calendar as recurring events with a real time - the marginal daily decision is what kills the habit, not the willingness.

Hair grows about 1 cm a month, so a 3 cm cut is roughly a 10-12 week cycle. Going shorter than the growth cycle means you see it every week, which is where barber-shop impulsivity lives - agree the length when you are thinking clearly, not when it is overdue.

A beard sits on skin that gets no sunscreen, traps moisture and harbours Malassezia, so itch and flake are usually seborrhoeic dermatitis of the beard - treated with the same antifungals as the scalp. Beard oil is mostly marketing; the diagnosis and the antifungal are what work.

Shave with the grain, use a sharp blade and a gel or cream rather than soap, and do not shave twice in a day. Every pass removes keratin and can cause folliculitis and post-inflammatory pigment, and in anyone who pigments the shadow is permanent unless treated as pigment.

Clean under the free edge weekly, cut straight across and file in one direction to avoid delamination, moisturise the nail plate rather than the cuticle, and leave the cuticle alone. A torn hangnail becomes an infection far more often than it becomes a cosmetic issue.
Brows - do not draw a shape and shave it

Brows do not regrow, and thinning the orbital rim ages the face faster than almost anything else you can do to it. Brush them upward, trim only obvious strays, and if you tint, stay two shades from natural so the roots do not read as a warm halo.

Twice-daily gentle cleanse, daily SPF, one retinoid and a moisturiser are the entire routine. Everything else is optional, and every optional step is another chance to quit the four that carry the result.
Book the dentist on the same calendar

A cleaning every six months with an exam attached. Periodontal bone loss is visible long before it hurts, and the mouth is the only part of you that cannot be managed from the kitchen - put it in the recurring events next to the haircut.

blurb: Energy balance, protein architecture, micronutrients, the graded supplement stack and physique aesthetics. No workouts - those live in GZCL Program.xlsx.

sections.title: Energy Balance - Nobody Gets This Exactly Right on the First Try
intro: Maintenance is an interval, not a number. Judge it on the 2-3 week weight trend and adjust once.
rows: kg x 31 kcal. Start here and correct against the trend rather than against a calculator.
kg x 34 kcal. The width of this band is the error bar on every other number in the module.
Calorie guidance - live from your goal
Reads PROFILE Goal and returns the band you are actually in, so the sheet changes when your goal does.
The deficit band that preserves lean mass and training output. Below it, the muscle cost arrives before the fat loss finishes.
A small surplus. A large one buys fat at a premium rate and hides the scale for weeks at a time.
Recomp - hold maintenance and eat protein high
Body composition changes without an energy change, which is slow, unglamorous and the only route that keeps everything else working.
At maintenance, adjusted by what the last 2-3 weeks actually did. Maintenance is an active number, not the absence of one.
Short sleep makes a deficit harder to run

Short sleep raises ghrelin, lowers leptin, raises insulin resistance and increases next-day energy intake - it moves the appetite side of a deficit before it moves the discipline side, and the next-day intake overwrites the deficit you planned. Fix the sleep before optimising the macros; the levers are on the SLEEP_RECOVERY sheet.
About 80% of calories from food you would recognise without a label, 20% from whatever you want. The 20% is what makes the 80% survivable for years rather than weeks.

Keep it to 0-1 a day. All-cause mortality RR 1.21 (95% CI 1.15-1.27), type 2 diabetes and anxiety OR 1.48, adverse sleep OR 1.41, obesity OR 1.55. Note that whole-grain breads are over-classified by NOVA - do not throw that subgroup away with the rest.
Alcohol is linear, not a J-curve

Per +8 g/day: all-cause OR 1.27, cardiovascular 1.30, cancer 1.20, digestive 2.06. Mendelian randomisation finds no protective benefit at low intake, so the observational curve is confounding, not protection. Least is best; never a reason to start.
Reverse diet 100-200 kcal at a time
Coming off a deficit, add 100-200 kcal/day rather than jumping straight to maintenance. Post-diet hunger is ghrelin up, leptin down, T3 down and thermic effect suppressed - not a broken basal rate.
A cheat day is not a metabolic reset
One high-carb refeed does not restart fat loss, and a large single-day surplus is net negative across the week it sits in. A diet break at maintenance is the useful version of the same idea.

sections.title: Protein Architecture
intro: The Value column is live: it reads the PROFILE derived cells, so the numbers follow your weight.
rows: Protein floor - live from your weight
1.6 g/kg bodyweight. The dose-response curve plateaus around here, which is why the floor and not the ceiling is the number to hit on a bad day.
2.2 g/kg bodyweight in a deficit; the studied range across trials is 2.0-2.7 g/kg.
0.4 g/kg, split across 3-5 feedings roughly 4 hours apart. Muscle protein synthesis saturates near 20-40 g a meal, so a single enormous dinner is the least efficient way to spend the same grams.
2.4 g/kg versus 1.2 g/kg, head to head

In a 40% deficit with high-volume training, 2.4 g/kg gained +1.2 kg of lean mass against +0.1 kg on 1.2 g/kg - and lost more fat (-4.8 kg against -3.5 kg). More protein was not more calories; it was a different result.
Protein in g/kg of lean mass
2.3-3.1 g/kg FFM when you are already lean and training hard in a deficit. This is the version that holds when bodyweight understates the tissue you are trying to keep.
Deficit size costs more muscle than protein dose
20-30% of weight lost on hypocaloric diets is lean mass, and the severity of the deficit drives that loss more than the protein does. Feed the target, then take the deficit smaller and longer.
Mostly unsaturated sources. Below the floor hormones, absorption and satiety suffer. Nothing here competes with the protein floor when energy is tight.
Carbohydrate is the variable, not the enemy
Whatever energy is left after protein and fat, typically 3-6 g/kg. It moves training quality, appetite and sleep more than it moves body composition on its own.
At least 30 g/day, a vegetable at every meal. High-fibre diets lower weight and visceral fat against isoenergetic low-fibre ones, and the satiety is what makes a deficit livable.
Repeated glucose and insulin spikes upregulate lipogenesis and hunger. Whole grains, legumes and fruit rather than white flour and sweets - same calories, different appetite.
Added fructose goes to the liver

If FattyLiver or Prediabetes is on your profile this is a direct lever: isoenergetic exchange of fructose for glucose raises liver fat and insulin resistance in controlled feeding studies. Cap the added kind; whole fruit is not the problem.
30-35 ml/kg/day, more in heat, more in a deficit, more when the sodium is high. Thirst and pale urine are the readout - you do not need to weigh your water.

It can suppress sleep through cortisol and glucose swings, narrows food variety, and opens real gaps in fibre, potassium and magnesium. If you run it, keep fibre at 30 g and watch sleep and electrolytes.

sections.title: Micronutrients That Actually Matter
intro: Test before you dose. Almost every row here is a reason not to supplement blind.
rows: Iron - ferritin and TSAT before anything

Never supplement iron without both a ferritin and a transferrin saturation. Ferritin is an acute-phase reactant, so read it with CRP; overload causes oxidative damage and it is not reversible by stopping.
Iron in women - the ferritin is confounded

Menstrual blood loss keeps ferritin low on a diet that would be sufficient for anyone else, so a single threshold misreads half the readers of this row. If the flag on your profile is Anaemia or LowFerritin, treat the result, not the number.
With no menstrual loss to drain it, iron accumulates silently and commonly surfaces in men from mid-life. Ferritin above 300 ug/L in a man is the trigger for HFE genotyping and a full iron workup.
Vitamin D - 1,000-2,000 IU, tested not dosed
Test 25(OH)D rather than dosing blind. Reported 30 ng/mL may truly be anywhere from 15 to 45 ng/mL depending on the assay, so the number you are chasing is less precise than it looks.
30 ng/mL is no longer a sufficiency line

The 2024 Endocrine Society retracted the 30 ng/mL sufficiency category. Stop treating a single threshold as a verdict; the assay spread alone is wider than most of the interventions people take for it.
The IOM upper limit is 4,000 IU/day and levels above 50 ng/mL are of concern for hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria. More is not better; the UL exists because people took more.
Vitamin B12 - test, and pair with MMA
Serum B12 alone misses deficiency. Methylmalonic acid is the second marker that separates a borderline result from a real one, and it rises before the serum does.
Leafy greens, legumes and liver cover the requirement without any of the upper-limit problem that high-dose folic acid carries in the general population.
Magnesium - correct a deficiency, not a mood

Evidence for improving sleep quality or mood in people who are not deficient is weak. If you are deficient, 200-400 mg of elemental magnesium in the evening is reasonable; if you are not, it is an expensive placebo.
Long-term high-dose zinc blocks copper absorption, and copper deficiency shows up as anaemia and neutropenia. Cap zinc above 30 mg/day or pair it with copper.
Chronic pyridoxine causes sensory neuropathy, dose-dependently and well below the old 100 mg caps. The EFSA tolerable upper limit is 12 mg/day for adults, and every label in a stack counts.
Iodine - the iodised salt is the whole story

The requirement is small and the population supply is one of the few good fortification stories left. Iodised salt plus whatever the diet supplies is enough; kelp and seaweed concentrates are how people overshoot into thyroid trouble.
Omega-3 - dose and formulation decide the outcome

If HighApoB or HighLpA is on your profile, this is the one supplement intervention with an outcome trial behind it: REDUCE-IT cut major cardiovascular events 25% on 4 g of prescription-grade EPA. VITAL and STRENGTH at around 1 g a day did not. The dose and the preparation, not the fish-oil idea, are the intervention.
Omega-3 for the skin - weaker case, say so
At ordinary doses the skin and inflammatory-marker evidence is thin compared with the cardiovascular data. Take the high-dose EPA route for the heart, not because the bottle mentions skin.
The requirement is in the hundreds of milligrams and a varied diet covers it. Large doses simply add to the fishy smell; there is no case for a standalone choline supplement.

Both too little and too much matter, and the upper limit is close to what a person might reach with a large daily serving of Brazil nuts plus a multivitamin. Food first, and count the nuts rather than the label.
High-dose beta-carotene in smokers increased lung cancer incidence in both CARET and ATBC. Take vitamin A from food; if you supplement at all, the regulated provitamin form is the safer ceiling.

sections.title: The Graded Supplement Stack
intro: Grade the use, not the molecule. Every row says what it is for and when to stop.
rows: The best-evidenced sports supplement that exists, and it is safe. Across 19 RCTs serum creatinine rose 0.13 mg/dL while eGFR did not move (-5.2, CI -15 to +4.6) and urea was unchanged - the creatinine rise is an assay artefact of higher muscle turnover, not kidney injury. If you do have kidney disease, monitor with cystatin C rather than creatinine.
Creatine does not cause hair loss

A 12-week RCT in 45 men found no difference in DHT, DHT-to-testosterone ratio, density, follicular unit counts or cumulative hair thickness. Do not skip the most effective supplement you can take because of alopecia.
It draws water into the muscle cell, not into the bloodstream. That is a training-output gain, not dehydration, and normal hydration habits are unaffected.
Whey and casein - the practical powder

High-quality, digestible and the easiest way to close the gap between food and the protein ceiling. Use them when the target is unreachable from food, not because whole food is inferior. A 20-40 g dose saturates synthesis; the rest of the day still has to come from somewhere.
Powder only if the target is missed from food

If you hit the protein floor from food on a normal day, a shaker is money spent on nothing measurable. The supplement is a solution to a shortfall you have already measured, not a default part of the protocol.
Caffeine - the cutoff is the whole intervention

The highest-yield item in this stack, and the only rule is when you stop rather than how much you take. The cutoff arithmetic, the 0, 3 and 6 hour findings and the no-tolerance result belong to SLEEP_RECOVERY, which owns the mechanism; the PROFILE cell computes your cutoff from your bedtime, so this row is the decision, not the derivation.
Vitamin D - dose after a test

1,000-2,000 IU/day is a reasonable maintenance dose once you know your level. The dosing rule and the retracted 30 ng/mL threshold are in MICRONUTRIENTS - this row only records that it is worth taking at all.
Omega-3 - prescription EPA, not a fish-oil capsule

The benefit arrived at 4 g of EPA in a pharmaceutical preparation; the 1 g studies were null. If HighApoB or HighLpA is set, match the formulation to the trial - or do not expect the trial's result from a supermarket capsule.
Magnesium glycinate at night, if deficient

200-400 mg of elemental magnesium in the evening, only where a deficiency exists. Magnesium L-threonate has small trials and no high-quality randomised evidence on sleep outcomes - low risk, low evidence.
Melatonin - 0.3-1 mg, timed to the clock

0.3-1 mg reproduces physiologic nocturnal melatonin levels - 0.3 mg and 1 mg both do it, and the common 5-10 mg is wildly out of proportion to the evidence. It works best 1-3 hours before sleep relative to your dim-light melatonin onset, not 30 minutes before lights-out. Fix light, caffeine and wake time first - a supplement does not repair a circadian problem.
Ashwagandha - the regulators have caught up

Multiple regulators now warn of rare severe liver injury, and it is contraindicated in known liver disorders. Avoid it entirely if any liver risk is on your profile; if you continue, monitor liver function rather than assuming tolerance.

Modest evidence for skin hydration and elasticity. Sun exposure is the dominant modulator of photoageing by a wide margin, so sunscreen and a retinoid come first and collagen comes fourth, at whatever price it sells for.

sections.title: Not Worth It
intro: Grade X across the board: no benefit worth the mechanism, the cost or the interference.
rows: If LowTestosterone is set on your profile, this is the row that matters most: tribulus, fenugreek, proprietary arousal blends and anything claiming to raise testosterone without a blood test move nothing. The interventions that do change a low level are diagnostic and supervised, and total testosterone alone misclassifies men with low SHBG - free testosterone, repeated in the morning, is the measurement that decides.

Caffeine and synephrine under a proprietary-blend label, sold on the back of an unblinded study. The mechanism is a stimulant effect you already have from coffee, with a hepatic and cardiovascular risk attached.

Branched-chain amino acids add nothing to a diet already meeting the protein target, because complete protein supplies them in the right ratio. A BCAA product is a way to spend money while missing the ingredient that does the work.

There is no defined toxin and no excretion pathway being accelerated. Twenty percent of US herbal supplement liver injury comes from exactly these products, green tea extract is the second cause, and with known liver risk this is the row that matters. Your liver clears most things at baseline.

Removing fat does not remove its calories and does not remove the reason you are hungry. The products are formulated to be eaten more of, which is the mechanism by which fat-free became the opposite of its name.

Unregulated, unapproved, unsterile products sold as regenerative medicine with no batch standard and no dose. The documented harms are infections, tumours and blood clots, not the promised regeneration.

EFSA finds no safe dose identified: at or above 800 mg of EGCG a day from supplements, transaminase elevation is associated with it. Brewed tea is a different and safe product. If you take the capsule, keep it well under that and never on an empty stomach.

sections.title: Body Composition
intro: The number is a measurement. What you do about it is decided on the PROFILE page.
rows: Body-fat band - live from your sex
Reads PROFILE Sex and returns the band where facial definition and hormonal function coexist. Change your sex on PROFILE and this cell changes with it.

The band where testosterone, appetite and facial definition are all still intact. Below about 8% the hormonal and recovery costs start to arrive, and the extra leanness buys very little you can see in a mirror.

The equivalent band sits higher, and the reason is not vanity: the same percentage in a woman means less lean tissue and a smaller margin above the level where menstrual function and bone density are compromised. Estrogen also decides where fat sits, so the shape at a given percentage is not the shape at the same percentage in a man.
Waist-to-height ratio - the one to actually track

Waist at the navel, height, and a target below 0.50. A practical screening cut-off for central adiposity that beats BMI, because BMI cannot tell muscle from fat and central fat is the compartment that carries the risk. The cell reads PROFILE live.

Useful for population screening and useless as a personal target: it cannot tell muscle from fat, and it is the same number for a lean frame and a heavy one. Live from PROFILE, kept because people will look for it.
Measure it the same way every time

Three-day average weight, waist at the navel at the end of a normal exhale, and one body-fat method only. Switching between calipers, a smart scale and a DEXA manufactures differences that do not exist - the estimate changes, the fat does not.

The live cell returns the body-fat percentage you entered if you measured one, and otherwise a circumference-based estimate from weight, waist and height. It is an estimate: a measured number beats it, which is why the PROFILE input exists above it.
Weekly loss ceiling - 0.4-0.6 kg a week

Read the kilograms: the live cell is a Goal-driven string, not a calculation - 0.4-0.6 kg for Cut, 0.1-0.2 kg for Recomp, and a dash for Bulk and Maintain. On your own weight that is roughly 0.5-1.0% a week, and past the top of it a fifth to a third of the loss is lean mass rather than fat.
Muscle protein synthesis falls, breakdown does not rise

In energy restriction muscle protein synthesis falls while muscle protein breakdown is unchanged (0.078 to 0.079 %/h). That is why a deficit does not automatically cost muscle - and why the deficit rate, not the deficit itself, is the variable that decides it.
Adaptive thermogenesis is real and small

A systematic review found it in 27 of 33 studies, but the well-designed ones return small or non-significant values, attenuated or absent after weight stabilises (-72 to -85 kcal/day, sustained). Count it as a 100-300 kcal/day penalty, not a broken machine, and re-measure maintenance instead of feeding the fear.

Each cut-and-regain cycle adds adaptive thermogenesis, increases the overshoot and produces net fat gain, while the skin and ligaments stretch and do not fully recoil. The slow deficit is not a compromise; it is the strategy that leaves you intact at the end.
A deficit stacked on high cardio volume

Concurrent training plus energy restriction carries the highest measured lean-mass loss of any combination - more than either alone. The volume that creates that condition lives in GZCL Program.xlsx; this row exists so the interaction is not discovered by accident.
Refeeding syndrome is a real risk at low intake

After prolonged severe restriction, fast reintroduction of carbohydrate can drive thiamine demand and fluid shifts. Rebuild at 100-200 kcal/day, include thiamine, and treat rapid refeeding after crash dieting as a clinical question rather than a challenge.

sections.title: Physique Aesthetics
intro: What the face and the silhouette actually do, and which of those things are not a diet problem.
rows: Chasing a face target is how you over-cut

The face is not a body-fat readout: facial fat is the last compartment to empty and the first to read as gaunt, so a scale that is moving and a face that is not is the normal state of a cut, not a failure of it. Use the waist and a monthly standardised photograph as the feedback, because a mirror in a deficit is a feedback loop that rewards cutting harder for a change that was never on the way.
The buccal pad grows with you

The buccal fat pad increases from childhood into adulthood and may not begin to decrease until 60-70, when it descends and pseudo-herniates. It is not a fat store a deficit reaches into: a cheek that stays full through a 15 kg loss is behaving exactly as described, and no further deficit empties it faster. The compartment anatomy is on the APPEARANCE sheet; what this row adds is that a full lower cheek is not a nutrition failure.
Submental and buccal - two different problems

They sit either side of the jawline and they end differently. The submental pad responds to total energy balance, empties late in a deficit and is what actually defines the jaw angle, so it is the compartment a cut can move. The buccal pad keeps its volume on its own schedule and, when it finally declines in later life, it descends rather than shrinks - a laxity problem at that point, not a fullness one. Treating the second like the first is why chin-and-cheek work comes back at the first sign of weight regain.

Sodium shifts fluid into the intravascular space. In controlled trials high sodium raised reported bloating with RR 1.27 while plasma volume rose dose-dependently and total body water did not - it is a distribution shift, not weight. Keep the evening meal lower-sodium, hydrate through the day, and never correct it by under-hydrating.

Alcohol suppresses the antidiuretic hormone, so the water lost overnight is replaced as rebound retention - which is why a face looks worse the morning after. Alternate with water, expect the effect, and judge nothing on a single morning.
A short night shows on the face before the scale moves

Objective skin measures move with a short night and observers rate it; the figures and the mechanism belong to SLEEP_RECOVERY. It is listed here because a deficit and a short night are one intervention aimed at two goals, and because the second one quietly undoes the first - see the sodium, alcohol and sleep compounding row below before judging a face on a single morning.
Sauna - a cardiovascular association, not a fat burner

Finnish cohorts reporting 4-7 sauna sessions a week against one or fewer showed cardiovascular mortality HR 0.50 and all-cause 0.60, observational and confounded by fitness and socioeconomic status. The sweat is the part that is not in question: sweat mass is water leaving the body, replaced within hours, and thermoregulation is not catabolism. Enjoy it for the relaxation and the plausible cardiovascular benefit; if you want an expenditure number, measure energy rather than reading a wet towel.

You cannot choose the site fat leaves from. Workout-induced local fat change is a transient measurement artefact, not a mechanism. The compartment that responds is decided by genetics and sex, and the only lever is the total deficit.

Anabolic steroids and corticosteroids drive sodium and water retention, redistribute subcutaneous fat and thin the skin - which is why a moon face arrives with the gyno, the acne and the shedding, not instead of them. It is a marker of drug exposure and it partially reverses on stopping.

Skin remodels over years after a large change in mass or fat, so the speed of the loss is the main determinant of how much laxity is left. Slower loss and the collagen support in the supplement stack are what help; significant laxity is a surgical question, not a diet one.
Stretch marks are hormonal as well as mechanical

Dermal tearing tracks puberty, pregnancy, Cushing syndrome and steroid use as closely as it tracks rapid weight change - which is why they appear on bodies whose weight never moved. Moisturise, and know that they fade with maturation rather than disappearing.
Sodium, alcohol and poor sleep compound

All three independently produce morning oedema, and alcohol also degrades the sleep that would otherwise clear it. Address one at a time and measure after two weeks rather than judging a single morning in a mirror.
No single food has a meaningful independent fat-loss effect outside of the total energy balance. Broccoli is a good vegetable; it is not a mechanism.

sections.title: Where Training Lives
intro: This workbook owns the numbers. GZCL Program.xlsx owns the programming.
rows: Sets, reps, load progression, exercise selection, weekly split and session structure belong to GZCL Program.xlsx and to nowhere else. Nothing in this module prescribes a workout, and if a row here ever looks like it does, it is wrong.
This workbook owns the targets GZCL executes against

The calorie band, the protein floor and ceiling, the per-meal protein, the weekly loss ceiling, the body-fat band, the caffeine cutoff and the sleep window. Set them here, then execute them in GZCL Program.xlsx against these numbers rather than against invented ones.

blurb: The one intervention that improves everything else. Wake time is the anchor, not bedtime.

sections.title: The Protocol - in This Order
intro: Wake time first. Everything else in this sheet is downstream of it.
rows: Fix the wake time, not the bedtime

The wake time anchors the circadian phase, the homeostatic sleep pressure and when you meet light. Hold it within 30 minutes every day, weekends included - a wake time that moves by two hours on Saturday has already cost you the week.
Morning light within an hour of waking

Ten to twenty minutes outdoors soon after you are up. Outdoor light is an order of magnitude brighter than any interior, and it is the signal that sets tonight's sleep pressure. Interior light through a window is a weak version of the same thing, which is why a winter commute is worth something.

Caffeine is an adenosine A1 and A2A receptor antagonist, so it blocks the pressure to sleep rather than causing wakefulness. 400 mg measurably disrupts sleep taken 0 h, 3 h or 6 h before bed - more than an hour of total sleep time lost even at 6 h - and habitual users build no tolerance to the effect. Half-life runs 3-7 h, so take the last dose five to six half-lives out: about 6 h for 100 mg, about 12 h for 400 mg. The PROFILE cell computes yours from your bedtime.
Evening caffeine moves the clock, it does not only block sleep

A double espresso three hours before bed caused a phase delay of roughly 40 minutes in dim-light melatonin onset - nearly half the shift produced by three hours of 3,000-lux bright light, for a fraction of the exposure. So an evening coffee is a circadian intervention as much as a sedative one, and no amount of tolerance training removes it.
Seven to nine hours is the target

The band is wide because need is individual; below it, chronic restriction independently raises insulin resistance, appetite (ghrelin up, leptin down), blood pressure and cortisol. Short sleep is among the strongest modifiable cardiovascular risk factors there is, and it is not a personality trait you can out-argue. If you are consistently under six hours, blaming genetics is the part to drop.
Core temperature falls before sleep onset and a cold room delays it. Around 18-19 C is the working figure; an unheated bedroom in winter is the commonest sleep-quality problem nobody logs.

Any light reaching the retina after dark suppresses melatonin, and the cheapest circadian intervention available is a light-proof bedroom. Eye masks and blackout fabric work if the window cannot be blocked; the light on the ceiling from a streetlamp is enough to matter.

The clock does not change because you decided to try harder, so give the transition the same discipline you give everything else. Read, breathe, whatever is low-stakes and repeatable - the mechanism is that pre-sleep arousal has to be unwound, and a chosen routine does that faster than an unresolved day does.
Alcohol is the classic sleep liar

It shortens sleep onset, which is the only number it improves. It suppresses REM, fragments the second half of the night as the metabolites clear, raises snoring and apnoea likelihood, and disrupts the circadian rhythm itself. Keep the last drink four to six hours before bed, and treat an eight-hour night with unrefreshing sleep as a reason to look at alcohol before anything else.

Light suppresses melatonin onset and content raises pre-sleep arousal, and both compound. No screen for the last hour, brightness down beforehand, and charge the phone somewhere else - the last half-hour of scrolling is the half-hour the light rule already covered.

The post-lunch cortisol dip is real and a short nap is a legitimate use of it. A late or long one removes homeostatic pressure you need that night, so it moves the cost onto sleep onset and fragments what follows.
One alarm - snoozing fragments the night

Each snooze is an arousal: homeostatic sleep pressure is reset downward and the deepest N3 sleep is the first thing lost. Get up with the first alarm and use the friction of standing up as the decision.
Light after sunset is the strongest circadian disruptor

Evening light displaces melatonin, delays the cortisol rhythm toward your wake time and suppresses evening testosterone. Dim or amber lighting after dark, and a dark bedroom, together do more for the rhythm than any supplement.

sections.title: Recovery Metrics - What Is Worth Measuring
intro: Trend and consistency, not stage detail. A consumer device is not a sleep study.
rows: Resting heart rate - the seven-day mean

Track the mean of a week of morning readings, not a single morning. Day-to-day noise swamps the signal; a drift over two to three weeks is the thing worth acting on, and it is a decent proxy for the sleep and illness load you cannot otherwise see.
HRV - trend only, and know the sensor

Heart rate variability is a genuine autonomic marker, but wrist optical sensors are not measuring the beat-to-beat intervals an ECG measures, so the absolute number is not comparable across devices or even firm to firm. Use the direction over weeks from one device, under one measurement condition.
Consumer sleep trackers - what they can and cannot do

Sensitivity is high at about 0.93: if you were awake, the device usually says so. Specificity is 0.18-0.54, so if it says you were asleep there is barely a coin-flip chance it is right, and MAPE - mean absolute percentage error - exceeds 20% for both deep and REM. One device called 59% of epochs deep when the true value was 10.8%. Fitbit overestimated total sleep time far more in insomniacs (+32.9 min) than in good sleepers (+6.5 min) - the worse your sleep, the worse the estimate.
How to use a tracker - consistency, not stages

Judgement: how consistently you go to bed, how consistently you wake, and how the trend is moving. Sleep-stage detail is noise at consumer accuracy and it invites the problem below. If insomnia or sleep apnoea is suspected, the device cannot answer it - a sleep study can.

Roughly 30.9% of US adults who track their sleep screen positive for orthosomnia risk, and about a third of adults track at all. The mechanism is feedback, not measurement: anxiety about a bad score produces the arousal that impairs sleep, and the next morning's score confirms it. The fix is a review window - monthly at most - then stop checking nightly, or stop tracking entirely. Waking at 87% every morning is data about the tracker.
Snoring, witnessed apnoeas and morning headache

With SleepApnea on your profile, no wearable substitutes for a sleep study. Loud snoring, witnessed pauses, a dry mouth on waking and a headache that clears by midday are the questions to take to a clinician, and untreated obstruction is a cardiovascular and dental problem long before it is a tiredness problem.
Social jetlag - over two hours, and the cost is real

A weekend shift of more than two hours against your weekday schedule was associated with +2.29 kg/m2 of BMI and 129% higher odds of a chronic condition; catch-up sleep beyond two hours carried 78% higher odds of being overweight. Circadian misalignment disrupts the HPA axis, so the cost is metabolic as well as cosmetic. Cap the shift under an hour and get outside in the morning.
Catch-up sleep does not repair the metabolic damage

Duration and circadian misalignment are different debts. Longer weekend sleep does not undo the phase shift, and the metabolic benefit of catch-up was confined to the most physically active quartile. Treat the schedule as the intervention; treat the weekend as part of the same schedule.

sections.title: When Sleep Reaches Hair and Skin
intro: The appearance sheet sends here for the mechanism; this is where the sleep loss actually shows up.
rows: The shed arrives 8-12 weeks after the insult

Hair is the lagging readout, which is why sleep belongs on this sheet and not only on the hair one. The insult - a bad fortnight of sleep, a crash diet, a hard month - registers now and the visible shed arrives 8-12 weeks later; the APPEARANCE sheet owns the timeline and the diagnosis, this row owns the reason a sleep debt can be the insult that triggers it. Do not read a sudden shed as a new event: it is usually the old one arriving on schedule.
Substance P is the sleep-to-scalp link

Substance P is the peptide that ties insomnia and stress to scalp tenderness, so a run of short nights is a plausible trigger for the tenderness rather than a coincidence of timing. The prevalence figures for trichodynia, and what to do about a tender scalp, are on the APPEARANCE sheet; this row exists because the mechanism runs through sleep, not because a scalp product will help.
Objective skin damage from a short night

Acute sleep loss produces less skin hydration, higher transepidermal water loss, higher skin pH, worse extensibility and more malondialdehyde - a measurable shift in the barrier, not an impression. It is one of the few appearance changes with a readable number behind it, and it reverses with recovery sleep.
Observers rate it before you do

Raters looking at sleep-deprived faces score them lower on attractiveness (-4% on a 100 mm scale), higher on tiredness (+19%) and lower on perceived health (-8.4 mm).
